Only the owner can cause ether to be transferred out of C (i.e., after a transfer attempt, address(c).balance decreases only if msg.sender == owner).

property_summary: For any payable amount and any receiver address, calling sendTo transfers the specified ETH out of the contract such that the contract balance decreases by that amount (the reference uses transfer which reverts on failure, while the mutant uses low-level call which can succeed or behave differently with a malicious receiver), and a malicious receiver that reverts on receive will cause the mutant to behave differently (mutant may not revert or may forward gas differently) — deploying a reverter helper shows the mutant breaks the invariant for some inputs.

For any sender and amount where the contract has sufficient balance, the reference C always reverts when the recipient's fallback/receive reverts (so the call to sendTo fails), whereas the mutant using low-level call can observe different success/failure behavior with a reverting recipient — the test asserts that calling sendTo to a deliberately reverting helper always reverts (ok == false) for the reference but the mutant will sometimes return ok == true.

For any recipient contract that reverts on receiving Ether and any amount, the reference C (which uses transfer) causes sendTo to revert (so the call does not succeed), while the mutant that uses low-level call may not revert (its success boolean can be true), breaking this invariant.

For every call to sendTo(receiver, amount) when the contract has sufficient balance and the caller is the owner, the reference contract always reverts if the receiver's fallback/receive reverts (i.e., sendTo cannot succeed against a reverting recipient), whereas the mutant using low-level call may observe a different success boolean and thus can succeed — the test deploys a reverting receiver and asserts that sendTo always reverts (ok == false).

For all caller addresses and amounts where the contract has enough balance and the caller is owner, calling sendTo to a recipient that does NOT implement a payable fallback/receive (an EOA-like or a contract with no payable fallback) always reverts in the reference (transfer will fail because transfer forwards 2300 gas and recipient's non-payable fallback will revert), whereas the mutant using low-level call may succeed for some inputs because call can invoke empty fallback without reverting — so the invariant: sendTo to a non-payable receiver always reverts; the mutant violates this for some inputs.

If the caller is the recorded owner then calling sendTo does not revert and preserves/decreases contract balance by exactly the sent amount (i.e., send succeeds), so a successful call implies no revert.
